label: DAILY EDITION
title: Three things worth knowing
subtitle: A new Parkinson’s treatment, an industrial steelworks carbon-capture trial and a €30.9 million worker settlement.

stories.title: FDA approved once-daily tavapadon for adults with Parkinson’s
stories.text: Juvmo (tavapadon) was approved as a once-daily pill, with or without levodopa. In a Phase III trial of patients with motor fluctuations, it increased daily “on” time without troublesome dyskinesia by 1.7 hours at week 26, versus 0.6 hours with placebo.
stories.why: It gives adults another oral option for managing movement symptoms. It does not slow or cure Parkinson’s; the evidence comes from company-sponsored trials, and reported adverse effects included nausea, dizziness, dyskinesia and hallucinations.

stories.title: A steelworks carbon-capture trial can collect 10,000 tonnes of CO₂ a year
stories.text: Shougang and Rio Tinto commissioned an industrial-scale trial at the Jingtang steelworks in China. The facility can process up to 3,000 cubic metres of blast-furnace gas per hour and capture up to 10,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually.
stories.why: It moves the technology from a smaller pilot into an operating steelworks. This remains a research facility, the stated capacity is not verified annual performance, and the captured volume is small relative to steelmaking’s total emissions.

stories.title: Builder committed €30.9 million after a Milan worker-exploitation probe
stories.text: Caddell Construction committed €30.941 million following an investigation at the new US consulate site. Nearly €20 million is intended for overtime, accommodation reimbursements and non-material damages, while the agreement also involves regularising around 500 workers.
stories.why: The settlement could deliver back pay and greater legal security to migrant workers. Payments were not yet complete when reported, the worker count came from sources familiar with the case, and the company said the commitment was not an admission of liability.
